Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:10:1.english: Because she is sustained by him - And his mind was on her earnings, which are frequent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:10:2.english: Which comes to her from the outside - And his mind was not on them to sustain her on their account.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:12:1.hebrew: בא זה ולימד על זה - מתוך שלא פירש נערות במקרא, אלא מאיליו הוא למד — שאין לנו דבר אחר לתלות יציאתו בו — הוצרך לכתוב שניהם. דאי כתב חד, הוה אמינא: בגרות הוא דאשמועינן קרא, אבל נערות לא מפיק לה. בא חבירו ולמד עליו: על כרחך חד מינייהו לנערות אתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:12:1.english: This [phrase] came and taught about that [phrase] - Since youth is not explicitly stated in Scripture, but rather it is deduced on its own — as we have no other factor to which to attribute her departure — it was necessary to write both of them. For had it written [only] one, I would have said: It is adulthood that Scripture teaches us, but youth does not release her. [Therefore,] its fellow came and taught about it: perforce, one of them comes [to teach] about youth.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:13:1.english: Just as it is with regard to a tenant and a hired worker - Which is written regarding *terumah*, to be expounded in this manner:

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:13:2.hebrew: תושב - האמור אצל תרומה: ״תושב כהן ושכיר לא יאכל קדש״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:13:2.english: A tenant - Which is stated regarding *terumah*: “A tenant of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat of the consecrated [food]” (Leviticus 22:10).

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:13:3.hebrew: זה קנוי קנין עולם - עבד עברי הנרצע ביד כהן, ואעפ"כ אין גופו קנוי לו כשאר עבדים כנענים לאכול בתרומה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:13:3.english: This [one] is acquired [as] a permanent acquisition - A Hebrew slave whose ear was pierced in the possession of a priest; and even so, his body is not acquired to him like other, Canaanite slaves, to eat of *terumah*.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:13:4.english: Acquisition of years - [One] for whom six years [of service] have not yet arrived.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:15:1.hebrew: בא שכיר ולימד על תושב - דעל כרחך חד מינייהו לנרצע הוא דאתא. ומאחר שנכתבו שניהם, משמעותא דנרצע מתושב אתיא — שהוא מיושב אצלו יותר מן הקנוי לשש שנים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:15:1.english: "A hired worker" came and taught about "a tenant" - For perforce, one of them comes [to refer] to a pierced [servant]. And since both of them were written, the meaning of a pierced [servant] derives from "a tenant" [toshav] — for he is settled with him longer than one acquired for six years.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:16:1.hebrew: התם תרי גופי נינהו - נרצע ושאינו נרצע שני גופים הם, ואפשר להיות שניהם בביתו של כהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:16:1.english: There, they are two bodies - A pierced [servant] and an unpierced [servant] are two [distinct] bodies, and it is possible for both of them to be in the house of a priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:16:2.hebrew: דכי נמי כתב רחמנא כו' - כלומר, ואפילו פירש הכתוב: "נרצע לא יאכל", וחזר ופירש על שאינו נרצע — ואף על פי שלא הוצרך לכותבו — הייתי יכול לתרץ ולומר: אף על גב דהוי שכיר מילתא דאתיא בקל וחומר, טרח וכתב לה קרא. לפיכך, כשכתבו התם, יש לומר: "בא זה ולימד על זה", ואין לנו להקשות: יכתוב נרצע בפירוש ולא יכתוב שכיר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:16:2.english: For even if the Merciful One had written, etc. - That is to say, even if Scripture had explicitly stated, "A pierced [slave] may not eat," and then explicitly stated [the same] regarding one who is not pierced — and even though it was not necessary to write it — I would have been able to answer and say: Even though [the case of] a hired worker is a matter that is derived through an a fortiori inference [kal va-chomer], Scripture took the trouble and wrote it. Therefore, when it wrote [them] there, it can be said: "This came and taught about that," and we cannot object: "Let it write [the case of] a pierced [slave] explicitly, and let it not write [the case of] a hired worker!"

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:17:1.hebrew: אבל הכא - דאפקה קרא מרשותיה בנערותה, לא משכחת לה אמה יוצאה בבגרות. והיכי כתב לן קרא מידי דלא הוי? לכתוב נערות בהדיא, ותו לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:17:1.english: But here - Since the verse removed her from his authority in her maidenhood, you do not find [a case of] a maidservant leaving at adulthood. And how could the verse write for us something that does not occur? Let it [just] write maidenhood explicitly, and nothing more.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:18:1.hebrew: אילונית - אין לה סימני נערות, ואשמועינן קרא שיוציאוה ימי בגרותה כשיהיה לה עשרים שנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:18:1.english: An ailonit - She does not have the signs of girlhood [puberty], and the verse teaches us that the days of her adulthood release her when she reaches twenty years of age.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:1:1.hebrew: יציאה דכוותה קא ממעט - יציאת אירוסין, דומיא דיציאת אמה, קא ממעט מדין אמה, ולמימר דיש כסף בה. ומה יציאת אמה העבריה — אין כסף לאדון דנפקא מרשותיה קאמר קרא, אף מיעוט דיש כסף דקא דייק ליציאת אירוסין — יש כסף למי שיצאה הימנו קאמר, והיינו אב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:1:1.english: It excludes a departure that is like it - [The verse] excludes the departure of betrothal, which is similar to the departure of the maidservant, from the law of the maidservant, to say that there is money in its case. And just as with the departure of the Hebrew maidservant, the verse says [that] there is no money for the master from whose authority she departs, so too, the exclusionary deduction that 'there is money,' which [the Gemara] infers regarding the departure of betrothal, means [that] there is money for the one from whom she departed — and that is the father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:20:1.english: Which do not release [her] from her father's authority - As we said above, that her earnings belong to her father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:20:2.hebrew: בגרות שמוציאה מרשות אב - דלא אשכחנא דזכי ליה קרא אלא נערות, דכתיב (דברים כב) לאבי הנערה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:20:2.english: Adulthood, which releases [her] from her father's authority - For we do not find that Scripture granted him [rights] except [during] maidenhood, as it is written (Deuteronomy 22): "To the father of the maiden."

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:20:3.hebrew: אינו דין כו' - ולקמן פריך: הא אמרן, מילתא דאתיא בקל וחומר, טרח וכתב לה קרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:20:3.english: Is it not logical, etc. - And later [the Gemara] asks: But didn't we say [that regarding] a matter that can be derived through an a fortiori inference, Scripture takes the trouble and writes it?

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:21:1.hebrew: לא נצרכה - קרא דבגרות, אלא ללמדנו שהאילונית נמכרת בקטנותה כשאר בנות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:21:1.english: It was not needed - The verse of adulthood [was not needed], except to teach us that an ailonit is sold in her minority like other daughters.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:2:1.hebrew: והא לא דמיא - יציאת אירוסין ליציאת אמה. והיכי קאמרת דיציאת אירוסין אתי למעוטי? הא לאו דכוותה היא, דאכתי לא נפקא מרשותיה דאב למעשה ידיה ולירושתה עד שתכנס לחופה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:2:1.english: But this is not similar - [Namely,] the departure of betrothal to the departure of a maidservant. And how can you say that [the verse] comes to exclude the departure of betrothal? For behold, it is not similar to it, since she has not yet left the authority of her father regarding her earnings and her inheritance until she enters the wedding canopy.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:2:2.english: With regard to the nullification of vows, at least, she leaves his authority - For he cannot nullify [them] alone.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:3:1.english: And she shall go out for nothing - And [Scripture] did not specify when she shall go out.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:3:2.english: These are the days of adulthood - When she changes from youth to become an adult woman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:3:3.hebrew: אין כסף - אלא דבר אחר מוציאה, אלו ימי נערות. ולקמיה פריך: מכי נפקא לה בנערות, בגרות מאי עבידתיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:3:3.english: Without money - Rather, another thing releases her — these are the days of youth. And later on [the Gemara] asks: Once she has left in youth, what is adulthood doing [here]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:4:1.hebrew: אן כסף - בלא יו"ד, כדכתיב ״מאן יבמי״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:4:1.english: En kasef [no money] - Without a yod, as it is written: “My levir refuses [me’en]” (Deuteronomy 25:7).

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:5:1.english: From where [do we know] that we expound - The [letter] yod of ein in this manner, on its own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:5:2.english: “She has no child” — I have [nothing] - That will prevent a daughter of a priest from eating terumah, except her offspring from an Israelite.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:6:1.english: Her children's children, from where [is this derived]? The verse states: "She has no [child]" — examine concerning her - For if her son died and he has a son, he too prevents her [from eating terumah].

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:6:2.english: Disqualified offspring - Such as a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:7:1.english: Children's children are like children - We derive this in Tractate Yevamot, in the chapter "HaBa Al Yevamto" (Yevamot 62b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:8:1.english: And the Tanna himself, from where does he [know] - That an without a yod signifies [negation] to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:8:2.english: Balaam refuses - He has no intention of going with us.

Rashi on Kiddushin 4a:9:1.english: And it was necessary to write [that] her earnings [belong] to her father - As [the Gemara] derived earlier from [the verse], 'his daughter to be a maidservant.'

Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:11:1.hebrew: ויצאה חנם אלו ימי בגרות אין כסף אלו ימי נערות - וא"ת: ברישא הוה ליה למנקט "אלו ימי נערות", והדר "ימי בגרות"? וי"ל: משום דאין כסף צריך לאוקמיה לימי נערות, כדאמר לעיל: "אבל יש כסף לאדון אחר", דהיינו ימי נערות — דאין האב זכאי בקדושי בתו בוגרת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:11:1.english: "And she shall go out for nothing" — these are the days of adulthood; "without money" — these are the days of youth - And if you say: First it should have stated "these are the days of youth", and then "the days of adulthood"? And one can say: Because "without money" must be established as referring to the days of youth, as [the Gemara] said above: "But there is money for a different master," which is [specifically] the days of youth — for a father is not entitled to the betrothal [money] of his adult daughter.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:12:1.hebrew: בא זה ולימד על זה - פירוש: אי לא כתב אלא חד, הוי מוקמי ליה בנראה יותר, דהיינו בגרות. וא"ת: ולמה לי "ויצאה חנם" ללמוד על "אין כסף"? הא ע"כ לא הוה מצינן לאוקמי "אין כסף" בבגרות, אלא בנערות — דהא מיניה דרשינן לעיל: "אבל יש כסף לאדון אחר, ומנו? אב!" אם כן, ע"כ האי קרא איירי בנערות, דאילו בבגרות אין האב זכאי בקדושין, דכיון שבגרה אין לאביה רשות בה. ואומר הר"ם: דאי לאו "ויצאה חנם", הוה מוקמינן "אין כסף" ויתורא דיו"ד דאמר רבינא — חד לנערות וחד לבגרות, ודרשה ד"אין כסף לאדון זה" לא הוה דרשינן; להכי איצטריך "ויצאה חנם":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:12:1.english: "This comes and teaches about that" - Explanation: If [the Torah] had written only one [phrase], we would have applied it to the more obvious [case], which is adulthood. And if you say: Why do I need "Then shall she go out for nothing" to teach about "without money"? For perforce we could not have applied "without money" to adulthood, but rather [only] to youth — for from it we derived above: "[There is no money for this master,] but there is money for another master, and who is that? The father." If so, perforce this verse is dealing with youth, for in adulthood a father is not entitled to [his daughter's] betrothal [money], since once she reaches adulthood, her father no longer has authority over her! And the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir] says that if not for "Then shall she go out for nothing," we would have applied "without money" and the superfluous [letter] yod that Ravina mentioned — one for youth and one for adulthood, and we would not have derived the exposition of "There is no money for this master"; for this [reason], "Then shall she go out for nothing" was needed.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:1:1.hebrew: יציאה דכוותה קא ממעט - פי' ר"ח: יציאת אמה העבריה מאדון, שהוא עת נעורים — אף כאן נערה. מיהו, סוגיא לא משמע כלל שהוא צריך ללמוד דביום נערות מיירי, אלא: מנלן דכסף דאביה הוי? ונראה לפרש "יציאה דכוותה": כגון ברשות אדון, אם היה שם כסף — אז היה נותן לאדון שיצאה ממנו; כמו כן כאן, שיש כסף ביציאתה מרשות אב — דאביה הוי. וכן משמע לשון הקושיא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:1:1.english: "It excludes a departure that is like it" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [Just as] the departure of a Hebrew maidservant from [her] master is at the time of youth, so too here [in betrothal, the verse speaks of] a young woman [na'arah]. However, the sugya does not at all imply that it needs to derive that it is dealing with the period of youth; rather, [the Gemara's question was:] from where do we know that the money belongs to her father [and not to her herself]? And it appears [correct] to explain "a departure that is like it": For example, in [the case of] the master's domain, if there were money [paid] there, it would then be given to the master from whom she departed; so too here, where there is money upon her departure from the father's domain, it belongs to her father. And so is implied by the wording of the [Gemara's subsequent] objection.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:20:1.hebrew: בגרות שמוציאה מרשות האב כו' - וא"ת: מיתת האב תוכיח, שמוציאה מרשות האב ואינה מוציאה מרשות אדון — אף אני אביא. ויש לומר דאיכא למפרך: מה למיתת האב שכן לא נשתנה הגוף — תאמר בבגרות שנשתנה הגוף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:20:1.english: "Adulthood, which releases [her] from the father's authority, etc." - And if you say: Let the death of the father prove [otherwise], for it releases [her] from the father's authority, yet does not release [her] from the master's authority — [so] I will also bring [adulthood, to argue that it does not release her from the master]! And it can be answered that it can be refuted: What [is true] of the death of the father is that her body did not change; would you say [the same] of adulthood, where her body did change?

Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:6:1.hebrew: זרע פסול מנין - אומר ר"י: זרע זרעה פסול קאמר — דהא כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה, פסלה מן הכהונה ולא תאכל עוד בתרומה. הילכך, ליכא לפרש זרע פסול ממש, אלא זרע זרעה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 4a:6:1.english: "From where [do we derive] disqualified offspring?" - The Ri says: It means [to say] the disqualified offspring of her offspring [i.e., a grandchild] — for once she has engaged in intercourse with someone disqualified to her, he disqualifies her from the priesthood, and she may no longer eat teruma. Therefore, it cannot be explained as actual [direct] disqualified offspring, but rather the offspring of her offspring.
